How each evaluation year was fitted

These are walk-forward figures rather than one model's: the model is refitted for each evaluation year on the seasons before it, so the result concatenates 11 separately fitted models and no evaluation year's outcomes appear in its own fit. This run did not record the year its training window starts, so this report does not name one.

Deltas in this report use model_minus_market_log_loss: race_multinomial_log_loss, where negative is better. That is stated because three delta fields existed in this repository and they did not all point the same way.

Provenance -- the source commit, the config and data digests, the environment and every input this report read by content digest -- is in the technical appendix and in run_lock.json beside this file. Canonical publication fails without it.

Evaluation population and market reference

The market reference

Every metric below is reported beside the market's own implied probabilities on the same races, normalised within each race. The delta is this model's race log loss minus the market's on the same races; negative is better.

The evaluation population

Every figure in this report covers the evaluation window beginning in 2016. 2015 is earlier than the window and is excluded from every evaluation figure below, including the bankroll paths. The feature-effect grid is the one exception, and says so where it appears: a learned response direction is a property of each year's fit rather than of the evaluation population.

Some years are warm-up rather than evaluation

2015 had no earlier year to fit a utility scale on and took the predeclared theoretical value (insufficient_history). The utility is divided by that scale, so those years amplify corrections where a fitted scale halves them, and their stakes and claimed edges are several times any fitted year's. They are excluded from every figure in this report and named here rather than labelled and left in.

Betting and bankroll analysis

Retrospective odds

Every stake, return and bankroll figure in this report is computed against historical result-page odds and official dividends. Those are not an executable pre-race price: they are the prices after the pool closed, and a bet placed at them could not have been placed. Nothing here establishes profitability. A profitability claim requires a locked model shadow-tested against timestamped pre-race odds snapshots.

Do not select a threshold from these returns.

Every year through 2026 has been used as development data in this repository: features were searched, architectures compared and thresholds inspected against these same seasons. The chronological split is real, so a test year is genuinely after its training rows, but no test year is unseen. Treat the forward figures as probability progress rather than as a locked out-of-sample result, and do not select a Kelly level or an edge threshold from this reused history. The confirmation step that this run cannot substitute for is a prospective shadow test against archived pre-race price snapshots.

Expected is the model's mean estimated return. Realised is official payout minus stake, divided by stake. Both are before rebate; rebate-aware sizing can change which bets appear, while credited rebates are reflected in the bankroll paths below. Read the pattern across bands rather than one band, because one winner can move a small group.

A negative-edge bucket appears only under rebate-aware sizing, and only at the larger fractions. That is the rule working as defined rather than a filter failing: the rebate is a cliff, so a runner whose own edge is negative can pay for itself by pushing the race's turnover over the threshold, and the stakes only get large enough for that at the higher fractions.

a fixed HK$10,000, so its bankroll fraction is what makes two scenarios differ

These are walk-forward figures rather than one model's: the model is refitted for each evaluation year on the seasons before it, so the result concatenates 11 separately fitted models and no evaluation year's outcomes appear in its own fit. This run did not record the year its training window starts, so this report does not name one. Each path is rebased on its own opening balance, so zero means break-even for every line from the same point. These curves are drawn from a bounded 998-point subsequence of up to 3,357 staked races, keeping each interval's highest and lowest balance so no peak or drawdown is smoothed away, and keeping the first and last points exactly. Every figure in the tables is computed from the full settlement, and the complete per-race path is in <code>race_paths.parquet</code>. Where a year is excluded, a continuous path opens at the balance the bank held when the kept years begin and an annual-reset path opens at the declared bankroll, so the two show different opening figures for the same rule. Rebate policy: 10% of the race net loss, once that loss reaches HK$10,000, as a cliff. Flat staking is omitted from these panels. Its stake is a fixed amount per bet and this settlement never halts on ruin, so its path can pass below zero -- a measure of how badly a rule loses rather than a balance an account could hold. It is also not a Kelly fraction, so it belongs to no preset. 2015 is excluded from every path below. These test years have no earlier year to fit the utility scale on and fall back to the predeclared theoretical value. The utility is divided by the scale, so the fallback amplifies corrections where a fitted scale halves them: their stakes and claimed edges are several times any fitted year's and are not comparable with them. Exclude these years from any return figure -- filter on is_honest_scale in the per-run CSV.

A day-block bootstrap: race days are resampled within each test year, so the interval accounts for clustering within a meeting, and the interval lies entirely below zero. It conditions on the fitted model and does not include refit uncertainty.

What a simulation cannot tell you

The model-assumed simulation draws winners from the model's own probabilities. If those probabilities are wrong the simulation is confidently wrong in the same direction, so it bounds sampling risk and says nothing about model risk.

Technical appendix and provenance

The utility scale

Fitted minimum
2.1063
Fitted maximum
2.3979
Theory
0.7797
the value theory predicts

The fitted scale sits above the value theory predicts, in every year: 2.106 to 2.398 against 0.780 (the scale the fallback year used, which is the predeclared theoretical value). Theory gets this wrong and the fit is what the report uses -- a scale asserted from theory would divide the utilities by too little, and at that value the market-relative candidate loses instead of winning. A run that took the theoretical value on faith would have reported the wrong sign, which is why the first year -- which has no history and falls back to it -- is excluded from the headline and labelled.

The generating source tree was dirty

This run's provenance records uncommitted changes, so the commit named above does not fully describe the code that produced these numbers. Treat the figures as indicative until the report is regenerated from a clean tree.

Every input this report read is listed in run_lock.json by content digest, together with the lock digest of the run that produced them -- which is what chains a published figure back through the report to the fit and from there to the feature table's own digest.

Limitations and the retrospective-odds warning

Retrospective odds, restated

Every stake, return and bankroll figure in this report is computed against historical result-page odds and official dividends. Those are not an executable pre-race price: they are the prices after the pool closed, and a bet placed at them could not have been placed. Nothing here establishes profitability. A profitability claim requires a locked model shadow-tested against timestamped pre-race odds snapshots.

Restated at the end as well as beside the betting numbers, deliberately. It is the single most load-bearing caveat in this report and the one a reader skimming for a return figure is most likely to miss.

Every test year is also development data

Every year through 2026 has been used as development data in this repository: features were searched, architectures compared and thresholds inspected against these same seasons. The chronological split is real, so a test year is genuinely after its training rows, but no test year is unseen. Treat the forward figures as probability progress rather than as a locked out-of-sample result, and do not select a Kelly level or an edge threshold from this reused history. The confirmation step that this run cannot substitute for is a prospective shadow test against archived pre-race price snapshots.

What else this report does not establish

  • It measures Probit Offset against the market on the evaluated races; it is not a cross-model comparison.
  • Its intervals condition on the fitted model, so they bound sampling risk and not model risk.
  • Every figure is out of sample in time but in sample in design: the feature set, the hyperparameters and the staking rules were all chosen with these years visible.
  • Nothing here is a shadow test. A profitability claim needs a locked model run forward against timestamped pre-race prices.
